title: Adding a service to a work order writes a note and audit entry
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a service advisor, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag). Open the audit trail wherever the build surfaces it for the asset/customer and check entries against the action you just performed.
  2. A work order to which a maintenance service is added from a schedule. Seed: create a work order from a worklist row (Create work order), or add a maintenance service to an existing work order.
custom_steps:
1. Add a maintenance service to a work order.
  2. Read the work order note and the audit entry.
  3. Look at whether the per-line origin tag is present or deferred.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Adding a service to a work order writes both a work order note and an audit entry, naming the schedule and service it came from.
  • Because the note and audit entry record the origin, a per-line tag is cosmetic and can be deferred.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10576 (S21, The audit trail); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S21; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

  • S21-E1: “Where the note and the audit entry record the origin, a per line tag is cosmetic and can be deferred”
